study.title: The Limbic-Prefrontal Network Modulated by Electroacupuncture at CV4 and CV12
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover fMRI study; each participant received electroacupuncture at both CV4 and CV12 with counterbalanced order
study.randomization: Order of acupoint procedures was counterbalanced (CV4 followed by CV12 in half of subjects; CV12 followed by CV4 in the second half); not described as randomized
study.blinding: Participants were in the supine position and unable to see the acupuncture procedures; blinding of participants to condition type not explicitly described; no mention of assessor blinding
study.population: Twenty one young healthy volunteers (22 to 28 years old, right-handed, 10 males)
study.inclusion_criteria: Young healthy volunteers; 22 to 28 years old; right-handed; free of major medical illnesses, history of head trauma, or use of medications within three days prior to the experiments; no contraindications for MRI scanning
study.exclusion_criteria: Major medical illnesses; history of head trauma; use of medications within three days prior to the experiments; contraindications for MRI scanning; subjects with sharp pain during EA (4 subjects excluded from sensory analysis; some subjects excluded from fMRI analysis)

arms.dropouts: 1 subject excluded from fMRI analysis due to sharp pain during EA at CV4; 1 subject excluded from sensation analysis for same reason
3 subjects excluded from fMRI analysis due to sharp pain during EA at CV12; 3 subjects excluded from sensation analysis for same reason

conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The description states needle retention without electrical stimulation, but does not specify insertion depth. It is unclear whether the needle was inserted to full depth (Level 1), superficially (Level 2), or merely in contact with skin (Level 3). The term 'needle in place' implies physical penetration, but the depth cannot be determined from the available description alone. | RESOLVED: needle inserted but depth unclear → assumed Level 1

extraction_notes.note: GLM activation/deactivation results for both CV4 and CV12 during EA are presented only in Figure 4 with MNI coordinates shown in the figure caption (X = 5). No coordinate table is provided for these results. Exact MNI coordinates for all activation and deactivation clusters are not reported in text or table format.

Local and distant functional connectivity maps for sham EA (Figure 5) and during EA (Figure 6) are shown as brain images only. No coordinate tables are provided for these comparisons. Region names extracted from figure captions and text descriptions only.

Sensory prevalence and intensity data (Figures 3a and 3b) are shown as bar charts only. Exact numeric mean values are not reported in the text for most sensation subscales (except for electric current amplitude and the fullness significance statement). Values were not extracted from figures to avoid hallucination.

Table 1 column headers are partially ambiguous in the PDF. The column 'Resting state (CV4)—True RS' appears to represent post-EA session compared to pre-EA resting state for CV4. Similarly for CV12. The 'CV4 versus CV12' columns represent direct comparison between the two post-EA conditions. This interpretation is supported by the text: 'Post-EA effects were derived by comparing the degree connectivity of post-EA session with the resting state session.'

Table 1 notation for 'Hp, HP' is ambiguous; this appears to represent hippocampus (Hp) and parahippocampus (HP) based on the table footnote abbreviation 'HP: hippocampus, ParaHP: parahippocampus.' However, the table header uses 'Hp, HP' together for what may be shared or adjacent coordinates. Both left and right coordinates are listed.

The 'Orbital F BA11/12' row in Table 1 shows values only for CV12 right column (16, 48, -12 with T=5.67) and another right column value (18, 48, -12 with T=3.09). It is unclear whether these represent separate peaks for CV4 post-EA and CV12 post-EA respectively or both from CV12. Based on table column alignment, the first entry (T=5.67) appears to be CV4 post-EA right hemisphere and the second (T=3.09) appears to be CV12 post-EA right. However, the left coordinate shows only values for CV4 (16, 48, -12). The orbital frontal row has been extracted accordingly.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures were not assessed or reported in this study. Prior acupuncture experience was not reported.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures (e.g., pain scores, symptom scales, quality of life) were reported in this study of healthy volunteers.

The paper states that during the post-EA period 'brain effects about 10 minutes after needle removal showed significant changes.' The exact timing of the post-EA resting state scan relative to needle removal is approximately 10 minutes based on this statement, but the exact interval is not precisely specified.

The Table 1 column labeled 'Resting state (CV4)—True RS' with left column coordinates and T-values appears to list peaks from the left hemisphere; right column entries are labeled 'Rt (MNI)'. Not all rows have bilateral peaks. For rows with only right-column entries (e.g., Orbital F), no left-hemisphere coordinate was provided.

Table 1 footnote lists 'Amygdala 24, -8, -20 2.5' for CV4 post-EA comparison column (CV4 versus CV12) with T=2.5, and also 'Amygdala 24, -8, -20 2.34' for CV12 resting state vs True RS right column. The same coordinate appears under both CV12 post-EA results and CV4>CV12 comparison. Both entries have been preserved as separately reported.

It is unclear whether the Orbital Frontal cortex coordinate row in Table 1 (16, 48, -12 / T=5.67 and 18, 48, -12 / T=3.09) refers to CV4 post-EA (left and right) or CV4 post-EA (left column) and CV12 post-EA (right column). Based on the table column structure described in the paper, the entry at 16, 48, -12 T=5.67 appears under CV4 post-EA right hemisphere and 18, 48, -12 T=3.09 appears under CV12 post-EA right hemisphere.

For Table 1, rows with only partial hemisphere entries (e.g., some rows have only a left or only a right coordinate listed) are extracted as individual separate entries. Blank cells in the original table are interpreted as not reported for that hemisphere.

The paper does not report the distant functional connectivity results from Table 1 in detail; only states 'slight changes in distant functional connectivity' for post-EA effects, without providing a separate table or coordinates for distant connectivity changes.
The table header in Table 1 contains the superscript 'ff' which appears to be part of 'effects' rendered as 'e ff ects' due to ligature OCR splitting. This has been interpreted as 'effects.'

It is not fully clear from the methods whether the resting-state sessions before and after sham EA were truly equivalent in terms of timing, or whether small motion-related or arousal confounds may differ. The paper does not describe motion exclusion thresholds explicitly.
